factions.Presidential Hopefuls: The 2028 draft class, and they're already running their own sets. Three of the four put distance between themselves and Trump within days of the loss (Vance flatly blamed the war; Hawley and DeSantis went after Senate leadership), while Rubio is the lone guy still setting screens for the boss.
factions.Media voices: The podcast-and-cable ecosystem that actually sets the movement's agenda, and it's splitting the fastest. Carlson declared the Trump era over and Shapiro called it a repudiation, Turning Point's Erika Kirk pointed to prices and the war but warned against infighting, and Hannity and Loomer stayed firmly in Trump's corner.
factions.Hawks: Peace-through-strength traditionalists, the wing most tied to the Iran war. Cruz called the night a Watergate-level repudiation and says the war has dragged on too long, Haley went full critic, and on Israel nobody here is giving an inch.
factions.Pragmatists and Dissenters: The told-you-so caucus of Republicans who kept Trump at arm's length all along. Christie declared "the Trump era is over," Murkowski wants Congress's war powers back, and Ayotte just showed you can survive a blue wave by running as yourself.
factions.Trump Loyalists: The franchise and its lifers. Their answer to a wipeout was promoting Stephen Miller and keeping Hegseth; even Trump's admission that the war and gas prices hurt came with an "emphatic yes" that he'd do it again. Budd, Landry and Reeves conceded the damage without blaming him.
factions.Tea Party/Freedom Caucus: The deficit hawks and libertarian gadflies, now leading the revolt against a quick leadership vote: Ron Johnson forced a debrief meeting with Lee and Rick Scott, and Chip Roy says Republicans "dropped the ball." Rand Paul blames deficits, tariffs and the war, and Massie is pushing Hegseth impeachment articles.
factions.New Right: The post-liberal, pro-worker, anti-H-1B wing that was supposed to inherit MAGA. Banks says there's "no way to spin" the loss and wants a frank reckoning before leaders are chosen, Moreno wants a "Last Supper" lame-duck sprint, and Schmitt has stayed on offense against Democrats instead of talking about the loss.
factions.Institutionalists: The leadership class and the governors who keep the lights on. Mostly they're hedging and lining up for minority-leadership jobs (Barrasso sees "clear lessons" but names no culprit); Lankford is the outlier, calling it a referendum on Trump and ICE, while Thune and Kemp actually moved closer to the party line.

boast.John Thune: Defended the record: taxes, border, Cabinet, judges.

field.h: The 2028 field is breaking. The Cabinet isn't.
field.b: Vance (−6.3), Cruz (−4.2), Hawley (−3.9) and DeSantis (−3.3) all moved away from Trump within days. Rubio, still in the Cabinet, is the only hopeful holding with him.

iran.h: The Iran war is the position they're abandoning.
iran.b: Nine Republicans from six factions broke with the war. The only four still defending it are Trump and his inner circle: Rubio, Hegseth and Sanders.

romney.b: Three are going harder, mostly on H-1B visas, and Chip Roy is doubling down on enforcement; only Lankford is pushing back, and only on ICE tactics. Like 2012's promised pivot, the leftward move isn't coming.

middle.b: Republicans scoring 8 or above on the Trump scale fell from 19 to 12, while those at 3 or below jumped from 5 to 13. The party is sorting away from Trump, not abandoning him.

prices.b: 17 of the 33 who gave a reason pointed to prices and cost of living; only 7 blamed Trump himself. Expect an affordability pivot, not a break with him.

tariffs.b: Three free-marketers from three factions (Cruz, Paul, Lankford) broke on tariffs, and not one Republican doubled down on them.

voices.h: The voices are outrunning the officials.
voices.b: Hosts and outside voices moved about twice as far from Trump as elected and appointed officials did, on average. The ideas tend to lead the votes.

senate.h: The Senate GOP is turning on its own leadership.
senate.b: Only 4 of the 18 Republican senators on the list have said nothing. Five pushed to delay the leadership vote, and 8 moved away from Trump; leader Thune moved toward him.

israel.b: Only Trump and Vance have shifted on Israel. The Hawks and Loyalists haven't budged from strongly pro-Israel, so the fight is at the top, not the base.

partners.h: Iran war powers is the biggest bipartisan opening.
partners.b: Nine Republicans who broke on the war map onto the Iran war powers measure, the most for any Agenda item. Tariff emergencies is next, with three.

field2.h: The 2028 field is breaking with Trump, except Rubio.
field2.b: Vance (−6.3), Cruz (−4.2), Hawley (−3.9) and DeSantis (−3.3) moved away, mostly by blaming his policies rather than him: Vance the Iran war, Cruz tariffs and the war, Hawley costs, DeSantis a do-nothing Senate. Rubio, still in the Cabinet, defended the war and holds at 10.

senate2.h: Senate Republicans want a reckoning first.
senate2.b: 14 of the 18 GOP senators on the list have now spoken, and 8 moved away from Trump, led by Lankford, Cruz and Hawley. Johnson, Lee, Rick Scott, Budd and Banks want a debrief before leaders are chosen. Only Thune moved toward Trump; Cotton, Schmitt, Wicker and Tim Scott are still silent.

bipart.h: Iran, corruption and tariffs are bipartisan openings.
bipart.b: The widest GOP breaks: the Iran war (9 Republicans across 6 factions), corruption and the Epstein files (6 across 5), and tariffs (3, with no defenders). The likeliest places for early deals.
